```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(catcheR); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)

## Folder layout -------------------------------------------------------------
##   analysis_EB/
##     scratch/   <- every input listed below
##     Output/    <- everything this document writes
SCRATCH <- file.path(params$analysis_dir, params$scratch)
OUT     <- file.path(params$analysis_dir, params$output)
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
show <- function(f, ext = "jpg") {
  p <- file.path(OUT, paste0(f, ".", ext))
  if (file.exists(p)) knitr::include_graphics(p) else invisible(NULL)
}
MAXR <- if (is.null(params$max_reads)) Inf else as.numeric(params$max_reads)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 9))
```

# The pipeline, and where this document sits in it

Four steps, in this order. Each one consumes what the previous produced, and
nothing here re-reads the FASTQ after the first step.

| # | step | reads | produces | needed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `catcheR_parsecatch()` | the two FASTQ pairs, `barcode_data.csv`, the barcode-to-gene CSVs | the `parsecatch` object (`.rds`), `complete_table_fin`, the 13 catcheR plots and the QC panels | every step below |
| 2 | `catcheR_parse_filtercatch()` | the object from 1 | `ValidCell` at the chosen thresholds, `cells_with_at_least_1_UCI.csv`, `new_cell_names.csv` | steps 3 and 4 |
| 3 | `catcheR_parse_nocatch()` | the object from 1 **and** the filter from 2 | the empty-vector cells, i.e. the unperturbed control set | step 4 (optional) |
| 4 | `catcheR_parse_seurat()` | the filter from 2, the empty set from 3, and split-pipe's DGE | the Seurat object with `catcheR_status` on every cell | your downstream analysis |

**Why the order matters.** Step 3 needs step 2 because an "empty" cell is
defined as one that is *not* in the called set: without the filter there is
nothing to subtract from. Step 4 needs step 2 for the same reason and step 3
only if you want the controls labelled rather than left as `not_detected`.

**What can be repeated cheaply.** Steps 2 to 4 all act on the object, so
re-filtering at new thresholds costs seconds and never re-streams the reads.
Only step 1 is expensive.

## Where the files go

```
analysis_EB/
  scratch/                       <- inputs, plus the handoff copies below
  Output/
    parsecatch/                  <- step 1: this chemistry's own folder
      filtercatch_p15_u1_r2_f20/ <- step 2, tagged with its thresholds
```

Step 1 nests under the chemistry name so that running the 10x or PIPseq
pipeline into the same `Output/` cannot overwrite these files - the 13 plots
carrying catcheR's own names have no chemistry in the filename. Step 2 adds a
folder named for its thresholds, so a second attempt at different values sits
beside the first instead of replacing it.

Three files are *inputs to a later step* rather than deliverables:
`cells_with_at_least_1_UCI.csv`, `new_cell_names.csv` and
`complete_table_fin_<sample>.csv`. With `to_scratch: true` they are copied into
`scratch/` as `<name>_parsecatch_<sample>.csv`, so a 10x and a Parse run can
share one scratch without colliding. The originals stay in `Output/`.

## One trap in the thresholds

`UMI.count` and `percentage` exclude with a strict `>`, `min.cell.UMI` includes
with `>=`. So `UMI.count = 1` keeps pairs of **two or more** UMIs, a UCI at
exactly 15% does **not** pass `percentage = 15`, and a cell with exactly 20
cassette UMIs **does** pass `min.cell.UMI = 20`. The floor keeps
applying by default: step 2 also defaults it to 20, so it stays in force unless
you pass another value (`0` disables it). This document passes it explicitly at
both steps, so the YAML header is the single source of truth.

# What this document needs

Everything lives in `scratch/`. This chunk is a guard: it fails here rather
than twenty minutes into a stream.

```{r inputs}
need <- data.frame(
  file = c(params$fastq_r1, params$fastq_r2, params$barcode_data,
           params$barcodes_genes, params$dge_mtx, params$dge_genes, params$dge_cells),
  role = c(rep("read 1 - carries the cassette", length(params$fastq_r1)),
           rep("read 2 - carries the cell barcode", length(params$fastq_r2)),
           "split-pipe barcode whitelist",
           rep("shRNA barcode -> gene", length(params$barcodes_genes)),
           "split-pipe count matrix (cells x genes)",
           "split-pipe gene table", "split-pipe called cells"))
need$exists  <- file.exists(file.path(SCRATCH, need$file))
need$size_MB <- round(file.size(file.path(SCRATCH, need$file)) / 1024^2, 1)
stopifnot(all(need$exists))
kable(need, caption = sprintf("Inputs found in %s", SCRATCH))
```

`barcode_data.csv` is not optional and cannot be reconstructed from the data.
Round 1 of the Parse barcode carries **two** sequences per well, one oligo-dT
and one random hexamer; in a 3' enrichment library the hexamer barcodes are
several-fold rarer, so a whitelist taken from the most abundant sequences
recovers only the dT set and silently discards the rest. Copy the file from
your split-pipe run (it sits beside the DGE output).

# Extraction

One pass per sublibrary. This is the only expensive step, so the chunk is
cached: re-knitting to adjust a threshold or a plot does not re-read the FASTQ.

```{r parsecatch, cache=TRUE}
res <- catcheR_parsecatch(
  folder            = SCRATCH,
  fastq.read1       = params$fastq_r1,
  fastq.read2       = params$fastq_r2,
  sublibraries      = params$sublibraries,
  barcode.data      = params$barcode_data,
  barcodes.genes    = params$barcodes_genes,
  set.names         = params$set_names,
  set.sizes         = as.integer(params$set_sizes),
  output_dir        = OUT,
  sample_name       = params$sample_name,
  called.cells      = file.path(SCRATCH, params$dge_cells),
  percentage        = params$percentage,
  ratio             = params$ratio,
  UMI.count         = params$umi_count,
  min.cell.UMI      = params$min_cell_umi,
  max.edit.distance = params$max_edit_distance,
  jitter            = params$jitter,
  max.reads         = MAXR,
  verbose           = FALSE)
# The entry point nests its outputs one level down, under the chemistry name,
# so another pipeline writing into the same Output/ cannot overwrite these.
# Take the path from the object rather than rebuilding it here.
OUT <- res$output_dir
res
```

## Where the reads went

```{r read-classes}
kable(res$read_class, caption = "Read fates")
kable(res$per_sublibrary, caption = "Per sublibrary")
```

The funnel below is the same information as a figure. Each stage is a strict
subset of the one above, so the bars are absolute read counts; the percentage
is of that sublibrary's own read pairs, never renormalised within a stage.

```{r funnel, fig.cap="Read fates per sublibrary and pooled"}
show("parsecatch_detection_funnel", "png")
```

## Which barcodes are cells

The knee separates real cells from the ambient floor. Comparing where it falls
to the cell count split-pipe itself called is the cheapest sanity check on the
whole extraction: the two are derived from completely different data.

```{r rank, fig.cap="Barcode-rank curve against the called-cell count"}
show("parsecatch_barcode_rank", "png")
```

## Would more sequencing help?

Answered by subsampling the reads that support each molecule, not by fitting a
curve and extrapolating. Read the marginal-return panel rather than the
rarefaction one: a curve that still rises slowly is not the same as a curve
worth paying for.

```{r saturation, fig.cap="Exact rarefaction and marginal return"}
show("parsecatch_saturation", "png")
```

```{r saturation-table}
f <- file.path(OUT, "parsecatch_saturation.csv")
if (file.exists(f)) kable(read.csv(f), caption = "Rarefaction, ten depth fractions")
```

## Construct geometry as the data confirms it

Read 1 is `[1 nt] rc(reference) rc(UCI) rc(barcode) constant ...`; read 2 is
`[UMI 10][bc3][linker A][bc2][linker B][bc1][poly-T]`. The cassette slice is
taken relative to the **vector constant**, not to the reference, which matters:
about 5% of cassette-bearing reads carry a sequencing error inside the 15 nt
reference anchor, and anchoring on the constant still recovers them with the
right barcode.

```{r geometry}
p <- res$params
kable(data.frame(
  field = c("reference", "empty reference", "vector constant", "UCI length",
            "barcode length", "UMI length", "linker A", "linker B",
            "barcode correction radius"),
  value = c(p$reference, p$empty.reference, p$constant, p$UCI.length,
            p$barcode.length, p$umi.length, p$linker.a, p$linker.b,
            p$max.edit.distance)))
```

# Choosing the thresholds

Yield is the wrong criterion here. Maximising the number of cells that receive
a call argues for no filter at all; what the filter is for is keeping the calls
*correct*. `catcheR_call_accuracy()` measures that directly: it takes the deep,
unambiguous cells as ground truth, subsamples each one down to a target depth,
re-applies the rule, and separates a wrong call from no call.

```{r accuracy, cache=TRUE}
acc <- catcheR_call_accuracy(res, min.truth.UMI = 100, output_dir = OUT, verbose = FALSE)
kable(acc, caption = "Wrong calls are far worse than missing ones")
```

```{r accuracy-fig, fig.width=5.2, fig.height=3.2}
long <- data.frame(
  depth   = rep(acc$UMIs_in_cell, 3),
  outcome = factor(rep(c("correct call", "WRONG call", "no call"), each = nrow(acc)),
                   levels = c("correct call", "WRONG call", "no call")),
  pct     = c(acc$correct, acc$wrong, acc$no_call))
ggplot(long, aes(factor(depth), pct, fill = outcome)) +
  geom_col(width = .65) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("correct call" = "#2E6E8E", "WRONG call" = "#B4432F",
                               "no call" = "#C7D3DC")) +
  labs(x = "cassette UMIs available in the cell", y = "% of reference cells",
       fill = NULL, title = "Below ~20 UMIs the calls stop being trustworthy")
```

The sweep separates the two opposite ways a cell fails. Lowering `percentage`
does not rescue cells that have no dominant UCI; it mostly turns them from
"no UCI passes" into "more than one passes", which is still not a call.

```{r sweep, cache=TRUE}
sw <- catcheR_threshold_sweep(res, percentage = c(10, 12, 15, 18, 20),
                              UMI.count = c(0, 1), min.cell.UMI = c(0, params$min_cell_umi),
                              output_dir = OUT, verbose = FALSE)
kable(sw[sw$UMI.count == params$umi_count & sw$min.cell.UMI == params$min_cell_umi, ],
      row.names = FALSE, caption = "At the chosen UMI.count and cell floor")
```

## Judged against the cells split-pipe actually called

The panels above count every barcode this package observed, ambient floor
included. The honest denominator is the cell list split-pipe called: here it is
fixed per panel, so a percentage axis does not mislead, and the absolute cell
count is printed above each bar anyway.

```{r called-comp, fig.cap="Clone composition of the called cells"}
show("parsecatch_called_composition", "png")
```

```{r called-floor, fig.cap="The UMI-floor panel restricted to called cells"}
show("parsecatch_UCI_per_cell_called", "png")
```

## Where to put the per-cell UMI floor

Left axis: how many cells still get a clone call. Right axis: the share of
those calls expected to be wrong, from the subsampling experiment. Note the
red curve is not monotonic at the far left - at 2-3 UMIs so few cells get any
call that the wrong-call share is small for the wrong reason. The decision
point is where it flattens.

```{r yield-error, fig.cap="Yield against expected error"}
show("parsecatch_yield_vs_error", "png")
```

## Clone composition against the per-cell UMI floor

Absolute counts, per sublibrary and pooled, with the total barcodes surviving
each cutoff printed above the stack. A rising "one clone" *share* means little
on its own; what matters is how many cells are discarded to achieve it.

```{r uci-per-cell, fig.cap="Clone composition at a ladder of per-cell UMI floors"}
show("parsecatch_UCI_per_cell", "png")
```

## What the two filter parameters buy

```{r diag, fig.cap="Call accuracy against depth, and the percentage sweep"}
show("parsecatch_call_accuracy", "png")
show("parsecatch_threshold_sweep", "png")
```

# Cell filtering

```{r filtercatch}
flt <- catcheR_parse_filtercatch(res,
  # the files a later step reads are copied into scratch/, renamed with the
  # chemistry and the sample, so several pipelines can share one scratch
  to.scratch   = if (isTRUE(params$to_scratch)) SCRATCH else NULL,
                                 UMI.count    = params$umi_count,
                                 percentage   = params$percentage,
                                 ratio        = params$ratio,
                                 min.cell.UMI = params$min_cell_umi,
                                 output_dir   = OUT, jitter = params$jitter,
                                 verbose      = FALSE)
kable(flt$filter_returns, caption = "ValidCell across candidate UMI.count values")
```

```{r stage2-plots, fig.show="hold", out.width="48%"}
show("2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_thresholds"); show("true_UCIxcell")
show("cellsxclone"); show("2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_ValidCells")
```

# Unperturbed cells

```{r nocatch}
noc <- catcheR_parse_nocatch(res, filtered = flt, threshold = 0,
                             output_dir = OUT, verbose = TRUE)
```

# Join to the split-pipe matrix

This is the only denominator worth quoting. The barcodes this pipeline
produces include ambient ones that split-pipe never called as cells, so a rate
computed over all observed barcodes overstates coverage.

`count_matrix.mtx` is written **cells x genes**, the transpose of the 10X and
PIPseeker convention, so it is transposed on load and `Seurat::ReadMtx()`
cannot be used.

```{r seurat}
obj <- catcheR_parse_seurat(res, filtered = flt, empty = noc,
                            mtx    = file.path(SCRATCH, params$dge_mtx),
                            genes  = file.path(SCRATCH, params$dge_genes),
                            cells  = file.path(SCRATCH, params$dge_cells),
                            sample_id = params$sample_name,
                            project   = params$sample_name,
                            output_dir = OUT, verbose = TRUE)
```

## Clone composition of the called cells

Absolute counts, with the number of cells split-pipe called as the reference
line. Percentages that renormalise inside each threshold bin hide how many
cells a stricter threshold throws away.

```{r composition, fig.width=8.4, fig.height=3.3}
meta <- utils::read.csv(file.path(OUT, sprintf("parsecatch_cell_metadata_%s.csv",
                                               params$sample_name)))
meta$sublib <- sub("^.*__", "", meta$cellID)
meta$UMI_total[is.na(meta$UMI_total)] <- 0
meta$True_UCIxcellID[is.na(meta$True_UCIxcellID)] <- 0
cls <- function(d) data.frame(
  category = factor(c("1 clone", "2 clones", ">=3 clones", "no dominant UCI", "no cassette UMI"),
                    levels = c("1 clone", "2 clones", ">=3 clones",
                               "no dominant UCI", "no cassette UMI")),
  cells = c(sum(d$True_UCIxcellID == 1), sum(d$True_UCIxcellID == 2),
            sum(d$True_UCIxcellID >= 3),
            sum(d$UMI_total > 0 & d$True_UCIxcellID == 0), sum(d$UMI_total == 0)))
dd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(split(meta, meta$sublib), list(both = meta)), function(d) {
  z <- cls(d); z$group <- NA; z }))
dd$group <- rep(c(names(split(meta, meta$sublib)), "both"), each = 5)
ref <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(split(meta, meta$sublib), list(both = meta)), function(d)
  data.frame(cells = nrow(d))))
ref$group <- c(names(split(meta, meta$sublib)), "both")
ggplot(dd, aes(group, cells, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = .6) +
  geom_hline(data = ref, aes(yintercept = cells), linetype = 2, colour = "#B4432F") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("1 clone" = "#2E6E8E", "2 clones" = "#D1A13A",
                               ">=3 clones" = "#B4432F", "no dominant UCI" = "#C7D3DC",
                               "no cassette UMI" = "#F0F0F0")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "cells split-pipe called", fill = NULL,
       title = "Clone calls on the called cells, with the cell total as reference")
kable(dd, caption = "Counts behind the figure")
```

# The thirteen catcheR plots

Written to `Output/` as both `.jpg` and `.pdf`, under the same names
`catcheR_10Xcatch` uses.

```{r plots, fig.show="hold", out.width="48%"}
for (f in c("barcode_distribution", "gene_distribution", "UMIxUCI", "UCIxcell",
            "percentage_of_UMIxUCI_dist", "2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count")) show(f)
zf <- list.files(OUT, pattern = "^UMIxUCI_[0-9]+_[0-9]+\\.jpg$")
if (length(zf)) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(OUT, zf[1]))
```
